**Finding submitted: deviation (LICENSE) — fallback-level cure proposed.**

- **Responsive clause:** § 2 Kubient License (p0002) is the sole grant to us; § 14(h) (p0072) assignment and § 6(a) (p0025) transfer/third-party-access prohibition were also checked, and "Customer" (p0000) is The Associated Press alone with no affiliate coverage anywhere in the document.
- **Why it fails fallback:** no affiliate coverage and no path to add affiliates (§ 6(a) bars third-party access absent Kubient's written approval), and the licence is expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable", so the specific licence terms defeat the general M&A assignment right in § 14(h).
- **Cure (one surgical replace):** grant extended to Customer "and, upon written notice to Kubient, its affiliates", and made "transferable to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition without Kubient's approval", with the removal of only the conflicting "non-transferable, non-assignable" words; all other grant language (including "revocable" and the sublicense restriction) preserved verbatim.
- **Noted, not flagged:** revocability and perpetuity sit only at the preferred level, so I did not volunteer them; the pre-existing mis-citation in p0021 ("license granted under section 3") is flagged in the rationale only.
